Pricing

How we price engagements.

No published rate card \u2014 pricing depends on scope, timeline, and what already exists. Here\u2019s how we structure it and how to figure out which model fits.

Best when the scope is clear

Fixed project

You know what you need built. We scope it, quote a fixed price for the full build, and deliver against that scope — no surprise invoices.

  • One clear price, agreed before work starts
  • Defined deliverables and milestones
  • Best for a product, MVP, or feature build with a known end state

Best for ongoing work

Retainer

A fixed monthly commitment for continuous engineering — new features, iteration, maintenance — without re-negotiating scope every time something changes.

  • Predictable monthly cost
  • Priority turnaround on requests
  • Best for products already live that need to keep evolving

Best for scoping or short work

Hourly

For work that’s too undefined for a fixed quote, or too small to justify a retainer — audits, advisory, or a short, well-bounded task.

  • Billed for actual time spent
  • No long-term commitment
  • Best for a scoping call, a code review, or a small fix

How we quote

What actually decides the number.

01

Scope

How well-defined the end result is. A clear spec quotes faster and tighter than an open-ended idea.

02

Complexity

A static site and a production ML pipeline with an API and CI aren’t priced the same way — the engineering underneath matters more than the surface.

03

Timeline

A compressed deadline costs more than a normal one, the same way it would with any studio.

04

What exists already

Building on top of an existing codebase or data pipeline is cheaper than starting from zero — we quote accordingly.

Not sure which model fits?

Tell us what you’re building. We’ll tell you honestly which pricing model makes sense \u2014 and a rough number \u2014 before anything is signed.
